label: GO step after a reward, with a strong but not saturated a1 preference, mid-episode (trials 10-59)
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2), only when the previous trial was rewarded (in_rew=0 at GO, prev_reward=1), and almost only when the agent is about to choose a1 with a strongly positive policy logit (choice > 8 holds 99% of mass; 2 of 12087 activations precede a2). It is restricted to episode trials ~10-59 and is silent from trial 70 on and in the first 10 trials, so it also depends on time in episode. The previous choice is nearly always a1 with a common transition (prev_action=2 or prev_common=0 gives about 3 activations), but adding that condition does not improve on the simpler predicate, since the high a1 logit already implies it. Inside the predicate it fires on only about 25% of steps (test precision is low), so something not captured here gates it further. It is not simply choice > 8: choice > 9 keeps only 49% of mass and choice > 9.5 only 3%, so it favours a confident but not saturated a1 preference. Uses no future variables: choice is the agent own policy logit at this step and ep_trial is elapsed time. No causal claims.
